title: Research: bind Callback.abort to parked-child interrupt invoice (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Independent audit binding Jose Manuel / jmbarrancoml’s PR2753/PR2809 `Callback.abort` stack/residue rollback to the NumericLease parked-child interrupt invoice. Open [#3999](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3999) audits NumericLease / SharedFrame interrupt alone and leaves Callback.abort as OQ1; this package answers that OQ with one composed fixture that fails inside a Callback while a lease is already parked in child phase.

At the pinned bytes: `Callback.abort` rolls residue/index to entry protected sets, rewinds program/fields tapes, and clears both faces of the `pending` and `values` Stacks (four Stack-role borrows); `Callback.close` rejects nonempty stacks; after abort, `lease.close(strict=False)` restores the parked parent. Three omission mutants show stack clear, residue rollback, and abort-not-close are load-bearing.

Complements open [#3999](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3999) (NumericLease/SharedFrame) and [#3993](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3993) (ScratchPool lease-end / CALL-empty on the successful path). Primary module is `controller.py` Callback, not `numerical_frame.py` or ScratchPool. Does not price park/restore machine steps and does not close a universal enclosing ownership argument.

**No new kappa.** Selected κ stays `0.001672660197076918`.

## Task and overlap

- Package: `research/selected-bit-callback-abort/`
- Tip: `29cfe0b3c292ba02cbbbfc01804c6b98858397ef`
- Base: `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`
- Scope: **refined** — Callback.abort composed with parked NumericLease child interrupt; answers #3999 OQ1

Closest priors: [#3999](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3999); [#3993](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3993); PR2809. Soft overlap vs #3999 is harness kinship on MiniArena/lease (~0.6–0.8 verify/test) with distinct Callback obligation (independent ≈0.28–0.41; #3999 had 0 Callback mentions). Semantic successor, not a NumericLease reprint.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/selected-bit-callback-abort/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -Werror -B research/selected-bit-callback-abort/verify.py
python3.12 -I -B research/selected-bit-callback-abort/independent.py
python3.12 -I -B research/selected-bit-callback-abort/test_package.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-bit-callback-abort
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_SELECTED_BIT_CALLBACK_ABORT parked_child_callback_abort stack_residue_rollback lease_nonstrict_restore three_mutants no_new_kappa
PASS_SELECTED_BIT_CALLBACK_ABORT_TESTS groups=6
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/selected-bit-callback-abort outcome=completed
```

Default verify is read-only. Admission uses `need()` and still fires under `-O`.

## Credit

Prepared by Wentao Li ([VictorLiwentao](https://github.com/VictorLiwentao), [@Is__Victor](https://x.com/Is__Victor)) with substantial AI assistance, under Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. Compose Callback.abort with ScratchPool lease-end / CALL-empty and residual/CALL into one enclosing ownership argument.
2. Supply a complete machine-step charge for park/restore on the interrupt path that includes Callback stack faces.
3. Does any selected GL64 coefficient path require Callback.abort under a parked numerical child with a nonzero continuation depth?
